label: Bible Study
prompt: Give, and it shall be given unto you; good _____, pressed down, and shaken together, and running over, shall men give into your bosom. For with the same measure that ye mete withal it shall be measured to you again.
verse: Give, and it shall be given unto you; good measure, pressed down, and shaken together, and running over, shall men give into your bosom. For with the same measure that ye mete withal it shall be measured to you again.
note: Pressed down, shaken together, running over — a grain-market picture of generous giving.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: For thus saith the LORD of hosts; After the glory hath he sent me unto the nations which spoiled you: for he that toucheth you toucheth the _____ of his eye.
verse: For thus saith the LORD of hosts; After the glory hath he sent me unto the nations which spoiled you: for he that toucheth you toucheth the apple of his eye.
note: The 'apple' of the eye is the pupil — the part you guard by reflex. That's how God guards His people.

label: Sunday School
prompt: And he received them at their hand, and fashioned it with a graving tool, after he had made it a molten _____: and they said, These be thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.
verse: And he received them at their hand, and fashioned it with a graving tool, after he had made it a molten calf: and they said, These be thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.
note: Aaron made a molten calf while Moses was up the mountain — later claiming it just came out of the fire.

label: Deep Water
prompt: Although the fig tree shall not _____, neither shall fruit be in the vines; the labour of the olive shall fail, and the fields shall yield no meat; the flock shall be cut off from the fold, and there shall be no herd in the stalls:
verse: Although the fig tree shall not blossom, neither shall fruit be in the vines; the labour of the olive shall fail, and the fields shall yield no meat; the flock shall be cut off from the fold, and there shall be no herd in the stalls:
note: Habakkuk lists total crop failure — no figs, grapes, olives or flocks — and the next verse still says 'Yet I will rejoice.'

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: For a day in thy courts is better than a thousand. I had rather be a _____ in the house of my God, than to dwell in the tents of wickedness.
verse: For a day in thy courts is better than a thousand. I had rather be a doorkeeper in the house of my God, than to dwell in the tents of wickedness.
note: A psalm for the sons of Korah, whose clan really did keep the temple doors — and preferred it to wickedness's tents.
